transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Sophia Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Stratus VP Eng), Maya Singh (Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (Infra), Priya Mehta (Procurement)

[00:00] Sophia Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round robin?
[00:06] Raj Patel: raj here, vp eng at stratus, we'll be owning billing and infra decisions for this project.
[00:11] Maya Singh: maya, head of ml, focused on model quality and inference cost.
[00:16] Tom Alvarez: tom from infra, curious about network/VPC options.
[00:21] Priya Mehta: priya procurement, mostly here to understand timelines and contract terms.
[00:27] Sophia Chen: perfect. i'm sophia with redwood, and with me is liam our se. goal today is to understand your workloads and cost targets so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:38] Liam Ortega: hi all, i'll dig into batching/caching and perf tradeoffs.

[00:45] Raj Patel: high level — we run a document summarization feature for enterprise customers. currently on internal endpoints that are expensive. Target: keep percost under $0.0009 per generated token on avg, with 95th latency < 250ms for interactive flows. Budget is tight first year.
[01:05] Maya Singh: sequence lengths avg 300 tokens, but sometimes up to 1k for long docs. QPS is spiky — 10 qps baseline, 80 qps peak.
[01:18] Liam Ortega: ok, good. question, are you comfortable with hosted if the unit cost meets target? or is data residency a blocker?
[01:25] Raj Patel: hosted ok for now, but if we get to scale we may want dedicated for predictability and cost. also need SOC2 and SAML.

[01:35] Sophia Chen: noted. quick primer on levers: per-token base pricing applies to hosted; dedicated is a commit model with predictable throughput and lower per-token compute. you can also reduce unit cost with batching, prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, and lower-precision quantized models. we'll walk numbers after you share workload.
[01:58] Maya Singh: can you explain caching? our app often sends the same doc preface plus user question.
[02:05] Liam Ortega: yes — prefix caching or KV cache stores the token states for the shared prefix across requests. if you have repeated doc context we can reuse KV cache so only the user prompt is computed live — that reduces tokens processed per request drastically. it's not perfect for all workflows, but for doc templates it's great.
[02:27] Raj Patel: sounds promising. how about batching — wouldn't that add latency?
[02:31] Liam Ortega: batching groups requests on the GPU. it increases throughput and reduces cost per token, but there's a latency tradeoff. we support dynamic batching with latency SLOs so you can cap max wait, and smart batching that prioritizes interactive flows.
[02:49] Maya Singh: any numbers — like what's the delta between hosted per-token and dedicated per-token after batching/caching?
[02:55] Sophia Chen: rough ballpark — hosted might be $0.003-$0.006 per generated k-token depending on model; with caching and batching you can see effective unit cost drop 30-60% depending on hit rate. dedicated upfront commit can reduce compute cost further — maybe another 20-40% at scale. these are very workload dependent.
[03:17] Priya Mehta: when you say commit, is that a monthly reserved capacity? what's the minimum?
[03:23] Sophia Chen: for Dedicated we do monthly or annual reserved capacity; min depends on GPU type and region — typical entry is 4-8 cards for a pilot. we'll send exact pricing tiers.

[03:34] Tom Alvarez: on private deployment — we have internal rules for PCI-ish data. would Redwood private run in our VPC?
[03:41] Liam Ortega: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem; control plane can be customer-managed for sensitive setups. there's an operational overhead and license model — usually for regulated verticals.

[03:55] Raj Patel: back to unit economics — our CFO wants a model: given our avg seq 300, 10 qps baseline, 80 burst, and 30% cache hit, can you show per-token$/month for hosted vs dedicated?
[04:10] Liam Ortega: we can. we'll need details like exact model size (LLM family), expected percentage of streaming vs full responses, and whether you can tolerate a slightly lower-quality quantized model. with those inputs we build a cost spreadsheet.
[04:26] Maya Singh: we currently use an open 13B with fp16. brave to consider a 4-bit quantized variant if quality stays acceptable.
[04:34] Sophia Chen: that's a good candidate — 4-bit quantization often cuts compute and memory and can reduce cost ~30-50% depending on kernels. we also support automatic fallbacks to higher-precision variants for regression cases.

[04:50] Tom Alvarez: networking — for hosted, where are instances located? regionally? we need EU data residency.
[04:55] Sophia Chen: hosted offers regional endpoints (us-east, eu-west, ap-south etc.). for EU residency we can ensure traffic stays in-region; for stronger controls Dedicated or Private gives you more guarantees.

[05:08] Priya Mehta: procurement question — what are typical SLAs for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[05:12] Sophia Chen: hosted has best-effort SLOs; Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in contract addendum. we'll include those in the contract template.

[05:22] Raj Patel: can you do a short worked example on the call? pick numbers and walk through hosted vs dedicated math.
[05:27] Liam Ortega: sure — assume model outputs 300 tokens per request. baseline 10 qps steady, 80 peak for spikes, month ~2.6M requests (10 qps * 3600 * 24 * 30 ~ 25.9M actually, so maybe we scale down — let's use monthly active: 5M requests). if hosted per-token is $0.000004 per token generated (i'm simplifying) then cost is 5M * 300 * 0.000004 = $6k/mo. if prefix caching reduces generated tokens by 30% effective tokens per request becomes 210 -> cost $4.2k. batching might reduce compute cost by 25% effective so hosted after batching+caching might be ~$3.15k. Dedicated: with reserved GPU commit the per-token compute unit could be 40% lower vs hosted, so ~$1.9k in same assumptions. these are rough but show the lever effects.
[06:20] Maya Singh: that helps. curious about cold-cache misses — do you keep long-lived caches per customer?
[06:26] Liam Ortega: we support per-customer cache with TTL controls. you'd need to provision memory on the serving tier; it's part of the config. if you have many unique docs cache hit will be lower.

[06:40] Raj Patel: about batching — you mentioned dynamic policies. can we prioritize low-latency interactive vs background batch and guarantee latencies?
[06:48] Liam Ortega: yes — routing policy supports tiering. interactive lanes have lower batch sizes and stricter wait windows, background can have large batches. Dedicated helps with strict p95 guarantees because you own capacity.

[07:00] Tom Alvarez: let's talk benchmarking — what do you need from us to run a realistic perf/cost test?
[07:05] Liam Ortega: sample payloads, seq length dist, a realistic QPS pattern (time series), preferred model binaries (13B fp16 and quantized 4-bit candidate), and whether you want streaming. we'll provide a load harness and metrics collection (we can run in our sandbox or on your infra for Private).
[07:24] Sophia Chen: action item — liam will send benchmark config, sophia will share pricing spreadsheet with assumptions (batch sizes, cache hit rates, GPU types).

[07:34] Priya Mehta: timeline — procurement needs to see costs and contract by Apr 10 to evaluate for budgeting.
[07:40] Sophia Chen: we can prioritize that.

[07:45] Raj Patel: a few security Qs: KMS integration, audit logs, SSO. do you support customer-managed keys?
[07:52] Liam Ortega: yes — KMS/HSM support for Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports encrypted at rest and can integrate with customer KMS for enterprise tiers. audit logs and RBAC supported; we'll send SOC2 docs.

[08:05] Maya Singh: any gotchas on model performance with quantization? we've seen hallucination increase in some 4-bit variants.
[08:12] Liam Ortega: correct — quantization can change behavior. part of the eval is running a quality suite over your prompts. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles that minimize quality regressions and fallback policies if quality drifts.

[08:29] Raj Patel: talk money — what's included in hosted price vs what are add-ons?
[08:33] Sophia Chen: hosted per-token price includes compute and basic observability. Add-ons: extended retention for metrics/logs, premium support, dedicated SSO integration assistance, and long-term retention for audit logs. Dedicated pricing includes baseline infra commit; add-ons similar. Private has a platform license plus support.

[08:52] Tom Alvarez: what's the pilot path you recommend?
[08:55] Liam Ortega: pilot approach: 1) small dedicated slice or hosted trial with production-like traffic for 48-72 hours 2) run benchmarks and quality checks 3) iterate on batching/cache configs 4) choose commit size for Dedicated or move to Private if needed.

[09:10] Maya Singh: we want to run a 48hr pilot on a representative workload and validate quality vs quantized model.
[09:17] Sophia Chen: perfect — we'll propose pilot plan and slot.

[09:21] (brief crosstalk)
[09:26] Priya Mehta: procurement — please include termination clauses for pilot.
[09:29] Sophia Chen: will do.

[09:33] Raj Patel: anything else?
[09:35] Sophia Chen: quick recap of next steps: pricing spreadsheet, benchmark config, schedule deep dive, and SOC2/network docs.
[09:42] Raj Patel: that works. thanks everyone.
[09:45] Sophia Chen: thanks — we'll follow up by email with docs and two proposed times for the deep dive.

[09:50] End meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: transcription had some mismatches on acronyms (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as 'K V cash') and occasional speaker attribution errors near crosstalk.
